title: Petrobras Q3 2026 Earnings Preview: PBR Results Preview
summary: Petrobras (PBR) Q3 2026 earnings preview: consensus expects $32.5B revenue and strong oil production. See what to watch this quarter.
body_markdown:
## Petrobras (PBR) — Q3 2026 Earnings Preview


### Key Factors to Watch This Quarter


Factor Details & What to Watch


Revenue & EBITDA Trends Consensus expects Q3 2026 revenue of **$32,528M** and EBITDA of **$17,131M** . Track YoY and QoQ growth vs. Q2.


Net Income & EPS Consensus for Q3 2026 net income not provided; EPS consensus is $1.24. Compare to Q2 and prior year.


Production Volumes Q2 2026 oil production was 2.7M bbl/day (+ **15%** YoY). Watch for sustainability and further ramp-up.


Refinery Utilization & Output Q2 2026 refinery utilization at **101%** FUT; diesel/gasoline output up. Monitor for continued high levels.


CapEx Execution Q2 2026 CapEx was **$5.3B** ; YTD **$10.4B** . Guidance is **$16.9B** ± **5%** for FY. Watch for acceleration or delays.


Operating Expenses H1 OpEx at **$11.7B** vs. FY plan of **$20.2B** . Monitor for cost pressures, especially logistics/freight.


Debt Reduction Q2 2026 gross debt at **$70.8B** , net debt **$60.4B** . Target is **$65B** by YE. Watch for progress toward target.


Cash Flow & Dividends Q2 2026 operating cash flow **$12.3B** (+ **50%** QoQ). Dividend policy remains **45%** of FCF. Look for payout news.


Guidance Updates Any revision to FY26 production, CapEx, OpEx, or debt targets.


Braskem Exposure Ongoing governance and capital allocation questions; watch for updates on restructuring or capital needs.


---


## Summary and Conclusions


- **Petrobras enters Q3 2026 earnings off record operational and financial performance in Q2 2026, driven by high Brent prices, record oil production (2.7M bbl/day), and refinery utilization above 100%.**
- **Consensus expects another strong quarter, with revenue of $32.5B and EBITDA of $17.1B, both up sharply YoY and sequentially.**
- **Key focus areas are the sustainability of production growth, ability to maintain high refinery throughput, and management of costs/logistics as OpEx trended above plan in H1.**
- **CapEx execution is on track to finish at the top end of guidance, with management emphasizing capital discipline and prioritization of high-return projects.**
- **Debt reduction remains a priority, with the company targeting $65B gross debt by year-end.**
- **Dividend policy is unchanged (45% of FCF), but management has signaled that extraordinary dividends are unlikely unless there is clear excess cash after investments and debt reduction.**
- **Braskem remains a watch item due to governance changes and potential capital needs, but Petrobras has reiterated it does not intend to consolidate Braskem’s debt.**
- **Year-over-year comparables are tough: Q3 2025 was already a strong quarter, but Q2 2026 set new records, raising the bar for sequential performance.**

## Guidance and Management Commentary


### FY 2026 Guidance (as of Q2 2026)


Metric Guidance / Target Commentary / Context


Oil Production Top end of range; >2.6M bbl/day "Production has remained above the top of the range, and we're working hard to exceed the target."


CapEx **$16.9B** ± **5%** "Expect to end the year at the top of the range."


Operating Expenses **$20.2B** "Expenses may exceed the projection if global market logistics costs and exchange rates remain high."


Gross Debt **$65B** by YE "Maintain our expectation of converging to **$65 billion** over the horizon of this plan."


Dividend Policy **45%** of FCF Extraordinary dividends unlikely unless clear excess cash after investments and debt reduction.

## Last Year’s Q3 Performance (Q3 2025)


- **Revenue:** **$25,020M**
- **EBITDA:** **$11,998M**
- **Net Income:** **$4,821M**
- **EPS:** $0.67
- **Oil & Gas Production:** 3.14M boe/d (record)
- **Refinery Utilization:** **94%**
- **CapEx:** **$5.5B**
- **Gross Debt:** **$70.7B**


**Q3 2025 was a strong quarter, with record production and solid financials despite lower Brent prices. The YoY comparable for Q3 2026 is tough, but Q2 2026 set new all-time highs, raising the sequential bar even higher.**


---


## Intra-Quarter Developments and Management Tone


- **Production:** Continued ramp-up of new platforms (P-78, P-79), with additional capacity coming online. Management is focused on maximizing output and efficiency.
- **Refining:** Utilization consistently above **100%** , with ongoing efforts to debottleneck and optimize for high-value products (diesel, gasoline, jet fuel).
- **CapEx:** On track to finish at the top end of guidance, with acceleration where value-accretive.
- **Costs:** Logistics and freight costs are a watch item; management is monitoring and may revise OpEx guidance if pressures persist.
- **Debt:** Active management, including prepayments and renegotiations, to accelerate convergence to **$65B** target.
- **Dividends:** Ordinary payout policy unchanged; extraordinary dividends unlikely in 2026 unless surplus cash is evident.
- **Braskem:** Petrobras now has more influence via a new shareholders’ agreement but does not intend to consolidate Braskem’s debt; capital allocation decisions will be made with shareholder value as the primary criterion.


---


## Conclusion


**Petrobras is coming off a record Q2 2026 and faces a high bar for Q3 2026. The most important factors for the upcoming report are:**


- Sustaining high production and refinery utilization,
- Managing costs amid inflationary pressures,
- Delivering on CapEx and debt reduction targets,
- Clarity on capital allocation priorities (especially regarding Braskem and international expansion),
- Any updates to guidance for FY26 and beyond.


**With Brent prices elevated and operational execution strong, expectations are high. Any signs of cost overruns, production hiccups, or negative surprises on capital allocation will be closely scrutinized.**
